subject: Physics
title: Kinematics (Motion in a Straight Line and in a Plane)
summary: Kinematics describes only HOW things move — position, velocity, acceleration — not the forces (that is Laws of Motion). Every measurement is made from a frame of reference; the ground frame is the default.
Distance is a scalar (path length); displacement is a vector (straight from start to end). Speed = distance/time, velocity = displacement/time. Instantaneous velocity = dx/dt, acceleration = dv/dt.
With constant acceleration the three equations (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) apply everywhere — free fall has a = g. If acceleration varies, use calculus or graphs (area/slope).

Motion in a plane = two independent 1-D motions. In a projectile horizontal velocity is constant and vertical acceleration is −g. In uniform circular motion speed is constant but direction changes, so there is a centripetal acceleration v²/r towards the centre.

Vectors are the language of this chapter: addition (triangle/parallelogram), resolution (A cos θ, A sin θ), dot product (a scalar, for work and angles) and cross product (a vector, for area and torque). Relative velocity v_AB = v_A − v_B solves river, rain and train problems.

formulas.name: Average speed and velocity
formulas.formula: v_avg = total displacement / total time;   average speed = total distance / total time
formulas.mistake: Don't take average speed as (v₁ + v₂)/2 — that holds only for equal TIME intervals. For equal distances it is 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂).

formulas.name: Instantaneous velocity and acceleration
formulas.formula: v = dx/dt,   a = dv/dt = v dv/dx = d²x/dt²
formulas.when: When x(t) or v(x) is given.
formulas.note: Use a = v dv/dx when v is given as a function of position — no t needed.

formulas.name: Equations of uniformly accelerated motion
formulas.formula: v = u + at;   s = ut + ½at²;   v² = u² + 2as;   s = (u + v)t/2
formulas.note: Fix a sign convention once (up positive ⇒ g = −10) and keep it for the whole problem.

formulas.name: Distance in the nth second
formulas.when: Distance covered only in the nth second.
formulas.mistake: This is the distance in the nth second, not the total in n seconds.

formulas.name: Free fall and vertical throw
formulas.formula: Max height H = u²/2g;  time to top = u/g;  total time = 2u/g;  returns with the same speed u
formulas.when: Objects thrown up or dropped (no air resistance).
formulas.mistake: At the top v = 0 but a is still g — acceleration is not zero.

formulas.name: Graphs
formulas.formula: slope of x–t = velocity;  slope of v–t = acceleration;  area under v–t = displacement;  area under a–t = Δv
formulas.note: Area below the axis in a v–t graph counts negative for displacement but positive for distance.

formulas.name: Vector resolution and unit vector
formulas.formula: A = A_x î + A_y ĵ + A_z k̂;  |A| = √(A_x² + A_y² + A_z²);  Â = A/|A|;  A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ
formulas.mistake: Check which axis θ is measured from — from the y-axis, cos and sin swap.

formulas.name: Vector addition (resultant)
formulas.formula: R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ);   tan α = B sin θ / (A + B cos θ)
formulas.when: Two vectors with angle θ between them.
formulas.mistake: Measure θ with the TAILS joined, not tail-to-head.

formulas.name: Dot (scalar) product
formulas.formula: A·B = AB cos θ = A_x B_x + A_y B_y + A_z B_z
formulas.mistake: The dot product is a scalar — never write its answer with î/ĵ.

formulas.name: Cross (vector) product
formulas.formula: A×B = AB sin θ n̂ = |î ĵ k̂; A_x A_y A_z; B_x B_y B_z|;   A×B = −B×A
formulas.when: Area of parallelogram = |A×B|, torque, perpendicular vectors.
formulas.note: Changing the order changes the sign; î×ĵ = k̂, ĵ×î = −k̂.

formulas.name: Relative velocity
formulas.formula: v_AB = v_A − v_B   (velocity of A as seen from B)
formulas.note: v_AB and v_BA are opposite; first decide whose frame you need.

formulas.name: River crossing
formulas.formula: Shortest time: head straight across → t = d/v_b, drift = v_r·d/v_b.   Shortest path (v_b > v_r): head upstream at sin θ = v_r/v_b, t = d/√(v_b² − v_r²)
formulas.note: Shortest time and shortest path are two different cases — read the question carefully.

formulas.name: Projectile on level ground
formulas.formula: T = 2u sin θ/g;  H = u² sin²θ/2g;  R = u² sin 2θ/g;  R_max = u²/g at θ = 45°
formulas.note: θ and (90° − θ) give the same range but different height and time.

formulas.name: Projectile path equation
formulas.formula: y = x tan θ − g x² / (2u² cos²θ);   velocity at any time: v_x = u cos θ, v_y = u sin θ − gt
formulas.mistake: At the top v_y = 0 but v_x = u cos θ remains — speed is not zero.

formulas.name: Horizontal projection from height h
formulas.formula: t = √(2h/g);  range = u√(2h/g);  speed at ground v = √(u² + 2gh)
formulas.mistake: Time of fall does NOT depend on the horizontal speed.

formulas.name: Uniform circular motion
formulas.formula: ω = 2π/T = 2πf;  v = ωr;  a_c = v²/r = ω²r (towards the centre)
formulas.when: Moving in a circle at constant speed.
formulas.mistake: Speed is constant, velocity is not — so acceleration is not zero.

formulas.name: Non-uniform circular motion
formulas.formula: a_t = dv/dt (tangential),  a_c = v²/r,   a_net = √(a_t² + a_c²)
formulas.note: Writing only v²/r is half the answer when speed is changing.

examples.title: A car accelerates
examples.problem: A car starting at u = 10 m/s accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. Final velocity and distance?

examples.title: Ball thrown up
examples.problem: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Maximum height and total time?
examples.solution: H = u²/2g = 400/20 = 20 m.  Total time = 2u/g = 4 s (2 s up, 2 s down).

examples.title: Distance in the third second
examples.problem: A body starts from rest with a = 4 m/s². Distance covered in the third second?
examples.solution: s_n = u + (a/2)(2n − 1) = 0 + 2 × 5 = 10 m. (The total in 3 s would be 18 m — a different thing.)

examples.title: All three projectile numbers
examples.problem: u = 20 m/s, θ = 30° (g = 10). Time of flight, maximum height, range?

examples.title: Crossing a river
examples.problem: River 100 m wide, water 3 m/s, boat 5 m/s relative to water. (a) Least time? drift? (b) To reach the point directly opposite?
examples.solution: (a) Head straight across: t = 100/5 = 20 s, drift = 3 × 20 = 60 m.  (b) Head upstream at sin θ = 3/5 ⇒ θ ≈ 36.9° (from the normal); resultant = √(25 − 9) = 4 m/s, t = 100/4 = 25 s.

examples.title: Dot and cross product
examples.problem: A = 3î + 4ĵ, B = î − 2ĵ + 2k̂. Find A·B, the angle between them and |A×B|.

examples.title: Point on a rotating fan
examples.problem: A point at radius 0.5 m rotates at 120 rpm. ω, speed, centripetal acceleration?
examples.solution: ω = 120 × 2π/60 = 4π ≈ 12.57 rad/s.  v = ωr = 6.28 m/s.  a_c = ω²r = 79 m/s² (towards the centre).

examples.title: Rain and umbrella
examples.problem: Rain falls vertically at 6 m/s and a man walks at 8 m/s. At what speed and angle does the rain appear to him?
examples.solution: v_rain,man = v_rain − v_man ⇒ magnitude √(36 + 64) = 10 m/s, coming from the front at tan⁻¹(8/6) ≈ 53.1° to the vertical. Tilt the umbrella forward by this angle.

examples.title: Distance from a v–t graph
examples.problem: A body goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s, stays at 20 m/s for 6 s, then stops in 2 s. Total distance and average speed?

topics.title: Frame of reference
topics.explain: Motion is always relative to an observer. A man in a train is at rest for himself and moving for the platform. A frame in which Newton's laws hold directly (no acceleration) is inertial; in problems the ground is taken as inertial.

topics.title: Uniform vs non-uniform motion
topics.explain: Uniform motion: equal displacements in equal times (a = 0, x–t a straight line). Non-uniform: velocity changes. In uniformly accelerated motion the v–t graph is a straight line and the x–t graph a parabola.

topics.title: Reading graphs
topics.explain: The slope of an x–t graph is velocity; if the curve bends upward the velocity is increasing. The slope of v–t is acceleration and its area is displacement. An x–t graph can never show two x values at one time, and speed is never negative.

topics.title: Scalars and vectors
topics.explain: A scalar has only magnitude (mass, speed, work, energy); a vector has magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force). Vectors add by the triangle/parallelogram law; subtraction = adding the reversed vector. The resultant of two vectors lies between |A − B| and |A + B|.

topics.title: Motion in a plane
topics.explain: x and y motions are independent but share the same time. That is why a projectile is solved as 'uniform horizontal + vertical free fall'. Position vector r = xî + yĵ, velocity v = dr/dt.

topics.title: Important projectile facts
topics.explain: At the top, speed is minimum (u cos θ) and velocity is horizontal. Complementary angles (θ, 90° − θ) give the same range. R = 4H cot θ. Range is maximum at 45°. Air resistance is neglected.

topics.title: Uniform circular motion
topics.explain: Velocity is tangent at every point; acceleration is towards the centre (centripetal) with magnitude v²/r. Over one revolution displacement and average velocity are zero, but average speed is 2πr/T.

topics.title: Relative motion problems
topics.explain: For distance between two moving objects, treat one as at rest and give the other the relative velocity — the problem becomes 1-D. Rain–man, boat–river, two trains — all use v_AB = v_A − v_B.

ratta: v = u + at,  s = ut + ½at²,  v² = u² + 2as,  s_n = u + a(2n − 1)/2.
Free fall from rest: v = √(2gh), t = √(2h/g).
Projectile: T = 2u sin θ/g, H = u² sin²θ/2g, R = u² sin 2θ/g, R_max = u²/g.
R = 4H cot θ;  same range for θ and 90° − θ.
A·B = AB cos θ;  |A×B| = AB sin θ = parallelogram area.
River: shortest time t = d/v_b;  shortest path sin θ = v_r/v_b.
